passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Our Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (MD&A) is intended to convey and promote understanding of management’s perspective regarding operational and financial performance for fiscal years 2025 and 2024. This MD&A should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8. “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this Form 10-K. For a discussion of our fiscal year 2024 results compared with our fiscal year 2023 results, please refer to Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" portion of the Company's 2024 Annual Report on Form 10-K, filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025. The following discussion contains trend information and forward-looking statements. Actual results could differ materially from those discussed in these forward-looking statements, as well as from our historical performance, due to various factors, including, but not limited to, those discussed in Item 1A. “Risk Factors” and “Forward-Looking Statements – Safe Harbor Provisions Under The Private Securities Litigation Reform Act Of 1995” and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Our operating results depend upon economic cycles, seasonal and other weather‐related conditions, and trends in government funding initiatives, among other factors. Accordingly, financial results for any year presented, or year‐to‐year comparisons of reported results, may not be indicative of future operating results. Overview CRH is the leading provider of building materials critical to modernizing infrastructure. With our team of 83,032 people across 3,961 locations, our unmatched scale, connected portfolio, and deep local relationships make us the partner of choice for transportation, water and reindustrialization projects, shaping communities for a better tomorrow. CRH’s connected portfolio supplies building materials across the construction value chain, better serving our customers’ needs and driving repeat business while making construction simpler, safer and more sustainable. This customer-centric approach combines our unique entrepreneurial culture, leading performance and local market knowledge with our value-added building products and services to be a valuable partner for customers across our end-markets. CRH’s leading positions of scale serve transportation and critical infrastructure, reindustrialization projects, and commercial and residential construction activity in North America, Europe and Australia. Financial performance highlights: CRH delivered another record performance in 2025 resulting in the following performance highlights (compared to 2024): • Total revenues increased to $37.4 billion, compared with $35.6 billion in 2024; • Net inc ome increased to $3.8 billi on compared with $3.5 billion in 2024. Adjusted EBITDA* increased to $7.7 billion in 2025 from $6.9 billion in 2024; • Net income margin was 10.1% in 2025 and 9.9% i n 2024. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: In addition to the other information contained in this Form 10-K, you should carefully consider the following risk factors before investing in our Ordinary Shares. The following risks are considered material to our business based upon current knowledge, information, and assumptions. The risks and uncertainties we describe below relate to future events, expectations, trends, and operating periods, are subject to change and are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties of which we are not aware or that we currently believe are immaterial may also adversely affect the business, financial condition, and results of operations of the Company. If any of the possible events described below were to occur, the business, financial condition, and results of operations of the Company could be materially and adversely affected. If that happens, the market price of our Ordinary Shares could decline, and holders of our Ordinary Shares could lose all or part of their investment. This Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from those anticipated in these forward-looking statements as a result of various factors, including (but not limited to) the risks described below and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Risks Related to Our Industry and Our Business Industry Cyclicality and Economic Conditions CRH’s business depends on construction demand, and construction activity is inherently cyclical and influenced by multiple factors, including global and national economic circumstances (particularly those affecting the infrastructure and construction markets), monetary policy, consumer sentiment, swings in fuel and other input costs, and weather conditions that may, individually or collectively, disrupt outdoor construction activity. Given the nature of our core products, many of which cannot be transported on a cost-effective basis over long distances, our operations are particularly sensitive to the economic conditions in the local markets in which we operate. In general, economic uncertainty and rising interest rates can exacerbate negative trends in construction activity, including when current and/or prospective customers are unable to obtain credit or issue bonds, which can lead to the postponement, delay and/or cancellation of projects, and an associated negative impact on demand for building materials and related services. With a significant proportion of construction activity undertaken outside (e.g. highway construction), demand for and the utilization of the Company's products and services such as cementitious materials, aggregates, asphalt, concrete, and concrete products can be highly seasonal in line with customer demand, and may additionally be impacted by acute and/or chronic changes in global and/or localized weather events/conditions. credit_strengths.text: CRH's scale as the leading building materials provider across North America, Europe and Australia underpins resilient revenue growth and record profitability, with operating income and operating cash flow both expanding over the annual trend series. This earnings momentum supports internal funding of capital programmes and distributions without straining the balance sheet.

Liquidity is comfortable, with the current ratio above the sector median and cash balances covering a meaningful share of near-term maturities. The debt maturity ladder is well spread, with no single year absorbing a disproportionate share of repayments, which reduces refinancing concentration risk.

key_risks.text: Construction demand is inherently cyclical and locally concentrated, and CRH's products cannot be transported cost-effectively over long distances. Management flags that economic uncertainty and rising interest rates can delay or cancel projects, while weather disrupts outdoor activity, making revenue and cash flow sensitive to conditions in each local market.

The debt note shows a large concentration of senior notes maturing within the next few years, alongside commercial paper and bank loans, and the overall debt stock has risen across the annual trend series. Refinancing this ladder at higher rates would lift interest costs and pressure coverage.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is solid but sits below the sector median, and net leverage is modestly above the sector median on a cash-netted basis. Headroom to the next leverage threshold is limited, so a moderate EBITDA decline or incremental debt-funded acquisition could push the indicative profile weaker.

Free cash flow covers only a modest share of debt, and after capital expenditure the surplus is largely absorbed by acquisitions and buybacks. This leaves limited cushion for debt reduction, meaning leverage improvement depends on EBITDA growth rather than organic deleveraging.

overall_credit_view.text: CRH presents an intermediate credit profile: scale, leading market positions and positive free cash flow are offset by cyclical end-markets, leverage modestly above the sector median and coverage below it. The maturity ladder is manageable, but refinancing and acquisition funding warrant monitoring.

Our forward view is that stable infrastructure spending and reindustrialization demand should sustain earnings, but shareholder distributions and bolt-on acquisitions will continue to absorb most discretionary cash flow. We would view a leverage increase toward the next threshold or a coverage decline as a negative development.

credit_strengths.text: CRH作為北美、歐洲及澳洲領先的建築材料供應商，其規模支撐了具韌性的收入增長及創紀錄的盈利能力，經營收入及經營現金流在年度趨勢序列中均有所擴大。此盈利勢頭支持資本計劃及分派的內部融資，而不會對資產負債表造成壓力。
流動性充裕，流動比率高於行業中位數，現金結餘覆蓋了短期到期債務的顯著部分。債務到期階梯分佈良好，沒有單一年份吸收不成比例的還款份額，這降低了再融資集中風險。

key_risks.text: 建築需求本質上具有週期性且集中於當地，而CRH的產品無法以具成本效益的方式長距離運輸。管理層指出，經濟不確定性及利率上升可能推遲或取消項目，而天氣會干擾戶外活動，使收入及現金流對各當地市場的狀況敏感。
債務票據顯示，未來幾年內到期的優先票據高度集中，同時還有商業票據及銀行貸款，而整體債務存量在年度趨勢序列中有所上升。以更高利率對該階梯進行再融資將推高利息成本並對覆蓋率構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率穩健，但低於行業中位數，而按現金淨額基準計算的淨槓桿率略高於行業中位數。距離下一槓桿率門檻的緩衝有限，因此適度的EBITDA下降或增量債務融資收購可能使指示性狀況轉弱。
自由現金流僅覆蓋債務的適度份額，且在資本開支之後，盈餘大部分被收購及回購吸收。這為債務削減留下的緩衝有限，意味著槓桿改善取決於EBITDA增長而非內生去槓桿。

overall_credit_view.text: CRH呈現中等信用狀況：規模、領先市場地位及正自由現金流被週期性終端市場、略高於行業中位數的槓桿率及低於行業中位數的覆蓋率所抵消。到期階梯可控，但再融資及收購融資值得監控。
我們的前瞻觀點是，穩定的基建支出及再工業化需求應可維持盈利，但股東分派及補強型收購將繼續吸收大部分可自由支配現金流。我們會將槓桿率升至下一門檻或覆蓋率下降視為負面發展。
